Abstract:

Fishing communities play an important role in the economy, livelihoods, nutrition, food security, and the preservation of culture. Their livelihoods and culture are at risk due to their reliance on and interaction with the environment, as well as climate change.

Fishing communities in India are at high risk due to the effects of climate change, including sea-level rise, cyclones, floods, coastal erosion, rising temperatures, heatwaves, and environmental degradation. Climate change affects their livelihood, food security, cultural identity, and harms their economic, natural, human, and social capital. Fishing communities in Odisha are more vulnerable to climate change. The stressors make their socio-cultural and socio-ecological systems more vulnerable, as their livelihoods and food security become less stable amid resource decline, reduced fishing days, and loss of traditional knowledge. And, adaptive systems are under more stress from rapid environmental changes, developmental interventions, market pressures, and governance constraints. &nbsp

However, it is not clear whether socio-cultural factors and resource sustainability are associated, and few studies have addressed the locally situated understanding of vulnerability. Such issues will help clarify the interconnections among traditional fishing communities&rsquo vulnerability, traditional ecological knowledge systems, and adaptation. The present study will examine vulnerability among fishing communities, their livelihoods, perceptions, and responses to events in fishers' daily lives, using both qualitative and quantitative methods in the Jagatsinghpur district of Odisha. It will help us to understand the fishing community&rsquos situated knowledge of climate change, vulnerability, and their capacity to adapt to this changing environment.

Keywords: Fishing Communities, Climate Change, Vulnerability, Adaptation
